transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?
My head has felt foggy lately. I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, and which volunteer I’ve already called. It’s frustrating.
How has your sleep been lately—do you feel rested when you wake up, or do you often feel tired and sleepy during the day?
I wake up tired even if I’ve slept. By the time I’ve washed up and made breakfast, I feel like I need to sit down again.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly at night or that you seem to stop breathing or gasp for air while you sleep?
I’m not sure. I live by myself, so there isn’t anyone there to tell me what I do in my sleep.
Have you noticed any recent weight gain or feeling unusually cold compared to before?
No, I haven’t gained weight. If anything, my skirts have gotten loose. Food just hasn’t sounded very good most days—I mostly pick at toast or soup.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless, or have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

I’ve lost interest in things I used to love. My watercolors, my tomato plants, line dancing, even watching the cardinals out back... they’re all still there, but I just can’t make myself care about them.
How long have you been noticing this combination of forgetfulness, tiredness, and loss of interest—days, weeks, or longer?
It’s been about three months now—the low, slowed-down feeling.
Do you find yourself unintentionally dozing off or falling asleep during the day, like while reading, watching TV, or sitting quietly?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m actually falling asleep during the day.
Over these past few months, have you been feeling unusually guilty, worthless, or down on yourself?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about myself in those terms.
Have you noticed yourself getting confused about the day or date, having trouble finding the right words when speaking, or getting lost in places you know well?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed those kinds of things or paid close attention to them.
Do you often wake up in the morning with a headache or a dry mouth?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I wake up with either of those.
Since this started about three months ago, would you say your memory and forgetfulness have been getting steadily worse, or have they stayed about the same the whole time?
It’s been getting worse, I think. My head feels foggy, and I keep mixing up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, even which volunteer I’ve already called.
On days when you feel a bit more rested or in a better mood, do you notice your memory and focus improve, or does the forgetfulness stay just as bad no matter how you're feeling?
It seems to stay bad regardless. My head is just foggy, and I still mix up appointment times, exhibit dates, and which volunteer I’ve already called.
Have you noticed any other changes, like difficulty with tasks that require planning or problem-solving, such as managing your finances or following a recipe you used to know well?
I’m having trouble keeping simple things straight. My head feels foggy, and I mix up appointment times, exhibit dates, and which volunteer I’ve already called.
When someone reminds you of an appointment or detail you'd forgotten, does it come back to you and feel familiar, or does it still feel completely new to you even after being told?
I’m not really sure. Sometimes it comes back a little when someone tells me, but other times I still feel confused about it.

When you're trying to learn something new, like a friend's phone number or a new recipe, do you find you can't hold onto it at all even right after hearing it, or is it more that your mind wanders and you have trouble focusing on it in the first place?
It’s more like my thinking is just foggy. I mix up simple things—appointment times, exhibit dates, even which volunteer I’ve already called.

Did you notice the memory and concentration problems starting around the same time as when you began losing interest in your hobbies, or did the memory issues actually begin first, before you started feeling this way?
I think it was around the same time. Things I used to love—my watercolors, tending the tomato plants, line dancing, even watching the cardinals out back—I just can’t make myself care about them now.
Over these past few months, have you had any thoughts of death, or that life isn't worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I’m not sure. I’ve been feeling low, but I don’t really know what you mean by thoughts of death.
Do you notice your mood and energy are worse in the morning and then get a bit better as the day goes on, or does it stay the same throughout the day?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern like that.
Are you still able to manage everyday tasks on your own—like paying bills, shopping, or cooking—or have you needed help with things you used to handle independently?

I’ve needed help lately. I’ve missed doctor appointments and gotten the senior center schedule so mixed up. My husband has had to help me make calls, keep track of the calendar, and deal with repair decisions I used to take care of myself.
Have you noticed any new physical symptoms lately, like weakness, trouble walking steadily, or changes in bladder control?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any new physical problems like that.
